# Sirach Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_006_page_001.jpg

---

1 Don't turn a friend into an enemy — a bad reputation is a source of shame and disgrace, and that's exactly what happens to people who talk out of both sides of their mouth.

2 Don't trust your own judgment so much that it tears you to pieces — like a bull left untethered.

3 Your leaves will be stripped, your fruit destroyed, and you will stand there like a dead tree.

4 A rotten soul destroys the person who has it and turns them into a joke for their enemies.

5 A pleasant manner makes you a lot of friends, and a gracious way of speaking draws many warm greetings.

6 Have as many good-natured acquaintances as you like — but your real counselors should be few; one in a thousand is enough.

7 Before you trust a new friend, test him first. Don't be too quick to open yourself up to someone.

8 Some people are your friend only when times are good — and nowhere to be found when things fall apart.

9 Some people who call you friend will become enemies, and then turn around and expose your private conflicts to embarrass you.

10 Some companions are great at the dinner table — but in the day of trouble, they're just not there.

11 While your life is going well, they treat you like their closest friend and feel at home with your household.

12 But the moment you hit hard times, they disappear and you won't see them for dust.

13 Keep your distance from your enemies — and keep your eyes open even with your friends.

14 A faithful friend is like a strong fortress. If you find one, you have found real treasure.

15 A truly faithful friend is beyond valuing. No price tag can be put on that kind of friendship.

16 A faithful friend is medicine that keeps you alive. Only those who fear the Lord will find one.

17 People who fear the Lord build real friendships, because like draws to like.

18 My child, start pursuing instruction while you are young — and you will still be finding wisdom when your hair is white.

19 Go to wisdom like a farmer going to his field — plow, sow, and then wait for a good harvest. The work will be hard at first, but before long you will be eating her fruit.

20 To undisciplined people, wisdom seems impossibly harsh. Those without sense simply cannot endure her.

21 She will lie on them like a heavy testing stone, and they won't take long to throw her off.

22 Wisdom earns her name — she does not give herself to many.

23 Listen to me, child. Take what I am saying seriously. Don't push my advice away.

24 Put your feet in her chains. Let her collar rest on your neck.

25 Stoop down and carry her. Don't let her restraints chafe you.

26 Come to her with everything you have. Follow her ways with every ounce of your strength.

27 Hunt her down, search for her, pursue her — and she will reveal herself to you. Once you've gotten hold of her, never let her go.

28 Because in the end, what you find is rest, and her presence will be turned into pure joy.

29 What felt like chains will become a fortress protecting you. What felt like a collar will become a splendid robe.

30 She wears golden ornaments; her cords shine blue and purple.

31 You will wear her like a glorious garment, and crown your head with her joy.

32 If you are willing, child, you can be taught. If you commit yourself, you will gain real understanding.

33 Love to listen, and you will receive instruction. Pay attention, and wisdom will grow in you.

34 Spend time with the elders. When you meet someone wise, make yourself their student.

35 Enjoy every conversation about what is holy. Don't let a wise proverb slip past you.

36 When you discover someone who understands things deeply, get to them early. Wear out their doorstep with your visits.

37 Think deeply about God's commandments. Meditate on his statutes day and night. He himself will sharpen your mind, and your longing for wisdom will be satisfied.
